name: Epoch Game Pocket Computer
description: A Japanese cartridge handheld made by toy company Epoch in 1984, five years before the Game Boy. It had a monochrome dot-matrix LCD rather than fixed LCD graphics, so it could run different games. High price and a tiny library made it a commercial failure.
curiosities: Only five cartridge games were released, plus two programs built into the console.
It launched at ¥12,800, close to the price of a Famicom.
Its built-in software included a puzzle game and a simple paint program.
It ran on four AA batteries for an estimated 60 to 70 hours.
story: Epoch released the Game Pocket Computer in Japan in 1984, one of the first handhelds with cartridges.
It had a black-and-white LCD screen and a few games.
It sold poorly and is now very rare.
